script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: Shards of Mercy

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A FAMILY gathers around their living room, the warmth of the fireplace casting shadows on their faces. At the head of the table, a father, JAMES, speaks.

JAMES
(serious)
I called this family meeting because I have something important to discuss. Something that has been weighing heavy on my conscience.

The room falls silent. The youngest child, LUCY, peeks at her older sister, EMMA, who rolls her eyes and smirks.

EMMA
(sarcastic)
Is it finally time to tell us why you've been looking so downtrodden lately?

James sighs, running a hand through his hair.

JAMES
(quietly)
Yes, my dear. I've been carrying a burden of guilt for far too long, and it's time I shared it with all of you.

INT. JAMES' OFFICE - FLASHBACK - MORNING

Years ago, James sits at his desk, looking distraught as he signs off on a business deal that will put many families out of work.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Back in the present, James' eyes meet those of each family member as he continues his confession.

JAMES
I made a decision that ruined lives. I allowed a company to expand at the cost of an entire community. I knew the consequences, but I chose profits over people.

The room grows tense as the family members digest the news.

EMMA
(outraged)
How could you do that to people? To us?

JAMES
(tearfully)
I can't change the past, but I can make things right. I will dedicate the rest of my life to making amends for the pain I've caused.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

James volunteers at the local community center, helping to rebuild a park that was destroyed during the expansion. He works alongside the very people his actions had hurt.

INT. LIVING ROOM - WEEKS LATER

The family gathers once more in their living room. The atmosphere is somber, but there is a sense of healing.

EMMA
(softly)
Dad, I've seen the way you've been working tirelessly to make things right. It's not going to erase the past, but it's a start. And maybe, just maybe, it will show others that no matter how far you've strayed, there's always a way back.

JAMES
(nods)
Thank you, Emma. Your understanding means more to me than you could ever know.

INT. COMMUNITY PARK - SUNSET

As the sun sets, James stands among the rebuilt park, surrounded by the grateful community members. He closes his eyes, feeling a sense of peace and forgiveness wash over him.

FADE OUT.

---

End screenplay.
